Real-time news, insights, prices, trending stories, and expert analysis - all in one place.Goldman Sachs Research Report Interpretation: October FOMC Will Skip a Rate Hike, December Is the Last OneGoldman Sachs expects the FOMC to skip a hike in October and deliver its second and final hike in December, bringing the terminal rate to 3.25–3.5%. This contrasts with market pricing, which implies four hikes and a peak near 4.55%.

Goldman attributes the entire 1.1pp overshoot in core PCE above the 2% target to three temporary factors: fading tariff pass-through, a limited incremental impact from the Iran energy shock, and mismeasurement of AI-related price pressure, which should peak around end-2026.

Financial conditions have tightened by about 30bp since September, roughly equivalent to slightly more than one hike but far less than the four hikes markets price. Goldman argues the FOMC will not view this as excessive tightening or as a substitute for hikes. The October meeting’s focus will be on statement language rather than policy action, with Goldman expecting wording similar to Jefferson’s, linking further adjustments to data trends, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks.

Goldman sees the March meeting as a high bar for another hike, as inflation pressures from tariffs, energy, and AI should fade. Risks to this baseline include higher oil futures, an escalation of the Iran conflict, and a larger January price effect. BofA Research Interpretation: Memory Stocks Trade at Only 2-3x 2027-28E P/E, the Cycle Has Not Turned Down | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsMarket AnalysisBofA Research Interpretation: ...BofA Research Interpretation: Memory Stocks Trade at Only 2-3x 2027-28E P/E, the Cycle Has Not Turned DownmarsbitPublished on 2026-10-20Last updated on 2026-10-20AbstractBank of America's October 16, 2026 report argues that memory stocks are mispriced. SK Hynix and Samsung have fallen over 50% from their June peaks, leaving them at just 2-3x 2027-28E consensus EPS—below the 4-7x seen in prior upcycles and near 1.0x 2027-28E book value, levels historically seen only at cycle bottoms. BofA maintains supercycle-level earnings forecasts: 2028 EPS declines only single digits YoY, with sales, operating profit and EPS still near 2027 peaks and record highs. So valuation prices a bottom while earnings show no downturn.

SK Hynix fell 57% from June to October, exceeding its 20-year average 51% drawdown, but in only 4 months versus the historical 15. Current DRAM ASPs are up 20-30% YoY, versus the 10-30% declines typical at bottoms. AI data center demand—LPDDR5, SOCAMM, HBM and eSSD—plus rising memory content per GPU/ASIC continues to drive growth.

Investor feedback is split: hedge funds bearish, most long-only investors bullish, with disagreement focused on cycle length rather than direction. Bear cases include neocloud borrowing costs, China 4F2 DRAM supply, falling memory per GPU, and slower AI capex. BofA rebuts each: valuations remain too low, China 4F2 impact is limited, AI backlog is large, and margins and ROIC stay high. Shareholder returns via dividends and buybacks could exceed 10% of market cap in 2027-28. BofA sees the storage TAM growing from ~$1.0tn in 2026 to over $2.0tn by 2030.

bonuses.requirements: Crypto Space Updates | HTX CommunityPostHomeFeedNewsRecommendFollowHotNewsArticlesCommunityAllCryptosStocksCommodities & FXMacro03:40BlackRock Partners with SBI and Startale to Explore Tokenized Funds and JPY Stablecoin InteroperabilityAccording to The Block, BlackRock Financial Management, BlackRock Japan, SBI Holdings, and Startale Group have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore the connection between tokenized money market funds and the Japanese yen stablecoin JPYSC. They will study the related technological infrastructure, business models, distribution channels, and regulatory requirements. bonuses.requirements: Sui Basecamp 2026: Record-Breaking 40 Million TPS, Sui Accelerates Toward the Agent Economy | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsSui Basecamp 2026: Record-Brea...Sui Basecamp 2026: Record-Breaking 40 Million TPS, Sui Accelerates Toward the Agent EconomymarsbitPublished on 2026-10-20Last updated on 2026-10-20AbstractSui Basecamp 2026 opened on October 7 at Marina Bay Sands in Singapore, with this year's flagship Sui ecosystem event themed around the "Agent Economy." The event drew founders, developers, and investors to discuss technology, witness new product launches, and try live demos. Key highlights included Samsung Wallet integrating USDC on Sui, the Hashi mainnet launching in phases this month, CCTP V2 going live on Sui, and Sui attempting to break its TPS record again. Mysten Labs co-founder Adeniyi Abiodun delivered a keynote titled "The Machine Economy Won't Wait," positioning Sui as the coordination and settlement layer for the Agent economy. He addressed SUI token supply, noting about 817,900 SUI had been repurchased this year, with future stablecoin revenue used to subsidize free stablecoin transfers and continuously buy back SUI, saying SUI may never reach 10 billion circulating tokens. Three major announcements followed: Samsung Wallet's USDC integration covering 82 million Galaxy devices in the US; CCTP V2 enabling native USDC cross-chain transfers between Sui and 29 other supported blockchains; and Hashi mainnet's phased launch this month with over $500 million in committed funding. A live TPS test, independently verified by CertiK, reached 40,614,180 transactions per second, setting a new record and signaling Sui is ready for the Agent economy. TSMC Q3 Signals: Significantly Increasing Investment in the More Mature 3nm Process, More Rational Approach to AI | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsTSMC Q3 Signals: Significantly...TSMC Q3 Signals: Significantly Increasing Investment in the More Mature 3nm Process, More Rational Approach to AImarsbitPublished on 2026-10-21Last updated on 2026-10-21AbstractTSMC reported strong Q3 2026 results, with revenue of NT$1,494.24 billion (about US$46.72 billion), up 50.9% year-over-year, gross margin of 66.4%, and net margin of 51.1%. Growth was driven by faster-than-expected 2nm shipments, which already reached 8% of revenue just two quarters after production ramp-up, as major customers including Apple, Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm, and MediaTek increased orders by 10–20%. Management raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to about 44% and plans to raise 2nm pricing by 3–6% starting January 2027.

Gross margin declined slightly quarter-over-quarter due to 2nm ramp-up costs but remains at a high level, with Q4 guidance of 65–67%. Capital expenditure remains aggressive: Q3 capex reached US$13.84 billion, up 42.7% year-over-year, and full-year 2026 capex is expected at US$60–64 billion, with 2026–2028 investment significantly higher than the past three years. TSMC is expanding 3nm capacity with new fabs in Tainan, reflecting the long lifecycle and strong demand for mature advanced nodes.

HPC products now account for nearly 70% of revenue. Meanwhile, TSMC remains cautious on High NA EUV, planning adoption around 2030, later than Intel and Samsung, prioritizing cost, maturity, and profitability over early adoption.
